findings.sourceReading: What are they, then? Bern questions the objects identity after calling them counterfeit.
findings.alternative: Who can express identity, but was it changes number and temporal frame; no past individual is the question here.

contexts.note: Complete documented111–225 tail review; parent verified173–174 and exact PC236754–236763. MG reference exchange proven yellow, independent of parent003 boredom subject. findings.sourceReading: Because I do not want to get bored with you. Their separate departures sustain Bern interest in Lambda.

findings.description: WH consistently renders 梅干 as dried plums without identifying the salt-pickled ume preparation. This loses the distinctive salty/sour food in Bern’s tea preference and recurring food jokes, and readily suggests an ordinary dried fruit instead.

contexts.japanese: 最高の紅茶と梅干を持って観賞に来るわ」
contexts.japanesePC: 「......紅茶に梅干を沈めてちょうだい。......まずい紅茶を飲みやすくするコツよ。」
contexts.japanesePS3: 最高の紅茶と梅干を持って観賞に来るわ」
contexts.WH: "......Please add some dried plums to some black tea.  ......That's the trick to making terrible tea drinkable."
contexts.MG: I'll come to watch, with some of the best black tea and dried plums."
contexts.UP: I'll come to watch, with some of the best black tea and dried plums."
contexts.note: Same umeboshi/dried-plums terminology; one canonical family. Exact three-witness recurrence quoted in reconciliation.

MG.japanese: 「その時、どんな顔を見せて絶望するのかしら。……くすくす、楽しみだわ。その際には私を呼びなさい。最高の紅茶と梅干を持って観賞に来るわ」
MG.translation: "When you do, I wonder what their faces will look like...as they lose all hope. ...*giggle* I can't wait. Call for me when that happens. I'll come to watch, with some of the best black tea and dried plums."

UP.japanese: 「その時、どんな顔を見せて絶望するのかしら。……くすくす、楽しみだわ。その際には私を呼びなさい。最高の紅茶と梅干を持って観賞に来るわ」
UP.translation: "I wonder what kind of expressions will register on their faces as they lose all hope? ......*giggle*, I can't wait. Call me when you do it. I'll come to watch, with some of the best black tea and dried plums."

findings.sourceReading: Umeboshi, or salted/pickled plums. MAFF explains the preparation as salt-pickling ume followed by drying: https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/traditional-foods/bunrui/tsukemono.html .
findings.alternative: Drying is part of preparation, so dried is not literally fabricated. However, the unqualified English term omits the defining pickling process and characteristic food identity. Count the recurring lexical loss once; the separate plum-pit action defect remains distinct.
